Search the juspay/hyperswitch repository and any relevant documentation or issues. I need concrete code examples, not explanations.

What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?

 Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in. Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

Learn More About The Payment Modules

- **Cost Observability** Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_ - **Revenue Recovery** Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_ - **Vault** A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_ - **Intelligent Routing** Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_ - **Reconciliation** Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_ - **Alternate Payment Methods** Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_
## Quickstart

Local Setup via Docker

```bash # One-click local setup git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch cd hyperswitch scripts/setup.sh ```
This script: - Detects Docker/Podman - Offers multiple deployment profiles: - **Standard**: App server + Control Center - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers - **Minimal**: Standalone App server - Provides access links when done If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker). 👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).

Hosted Sandbox (No Setup Required)

Hyperswitch offers a fully hosted sandbox environment that requires no setup. You can explore the Control Center, configure payment connectors, and test payments directly from the UI.

Architectural Overview

 ## Why Hyperswitch? Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations. Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are. “Linux for Payments” — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack. 205:             billing_name.clone(),
206:             payment_method_billing_address,
207:             business_profile,

210:             vault_operation.clone(),
211:             payment_method_info.clone(),
212:             payment_data.payment_method_token.clone(),
213:         ));
214: 
215:         let is_connector_mandate = resp.request.customer_acceptance.is_some()
216:             && matches!(
217:                 resp.request.setup_future_usage,
218:                 Some(enums::FutureUsage::OffSession)
219:             );
220: 
221:         let is_legacy_mandate = resp.request.setup_mandate_details.is_some()
222:             && matches!(
223:                 resp.request.setup_future_usage,
224:                 Some(enums::FutureUsage::OffSession)
225:             );
226:         let storage_scheme = platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme;
227:         if is_legacy_mandate {
228:             // Mandate is created on the application side and at the connector.
229:             let tokenization::SavePaymentMethodDataResponse {
230:                 payment_method_id, ..
231:             } = save_payment_call_future.await?;
232: 
233:             let mandate_id = mandate::mandate_procedure(
234:                 state,
235:                 resp,
236:                 &customer_id.clone(),
237:                 payment_method_id.clone(),
238:                 merchant_connector_id.clone(),
239:                 platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
240:                 payment_data.payment_intent.get_id(),
241:             )
242:             .await?;
243:             payment_data.payment_attempt.payment_method_id = payment_method_id;
244:             payment_data.payment_attempt.mandate_id = mandate_id;
245: 
246:             Ok(())
247:         } else if is_connector_mandate {
248:             // The mandate is created on connector's end.
249:             let save_payment_call_response = save_payment_call_future.await;
250:             match save_payment_call_response {
251:                 Ok(tokenization::SavePaymentMethodDataResponse {
252:                     payment_method_id,
253:                     connector_mandate_reference_id,
254:                     ..
255:                 }) => {
256:                     payment_data.payment_method_info = if let Some(payment_method_id) =
257:                         &payment_method_id
258:                     {
259:                         match state
260:                             .store
261:                             .find_payment_method(
262:                                 platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
263:                                 payment_method_id,
264:                                 storage_scheme,
265:                             )
266:                             .await
267:                         {
268:                             Ok(payment_method) => Some(payment_method),
269:                             Err(error) => {
270:                                 if error.current_context().is_db_not_found() {
271:                                     logger::info!("Payment Method not found in db {:?}", error);
272:                                     None
273:                                 } else {
274:                                     Err(error)
275:                                         .change_context(
276:                                             errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError,
277:                                         )
278:                                         .attach_printable("Error retrieving payment method from db")
279:                                         .map_err(|err| logger::error!(payment_method_retrieve=?err))
280:                                         .ok()
281:                                 }
282:                             }
283:                         }
284:                     } else {
285:                         None
286:                     };
287:                     payment_data.payment_attempt.payment_method_id = payment_method_id;
288:                     payment_data.payment_attempt.connector_mandate_detail =
289:                         connector_mandate_reference_id
290:                             .clone()
291:                             .map(ForeignFrom::foreign_from);
292:                     payment_data.set_mandate_id(api_models::payments::MandateIds {
293:                         mandate_id: None,
294:                         mandate_reference_id: connector_mandate_reference_id.map(
295:                             |connector_mandate_id| {
296:                                 MandateReferenceId::ConnectorMandateId(connector_mandate_id)
297:                             },
298:                         ),
299:                     })
300:                 }
301:                 Err(err) => {
302:                     logger::error!("Error while storing the payment method in locker {:?}", err);
303:                 }
304:             }
305:             Ok(())
306:         } else if should_avoid_saving {
307:             if let Some(pm_info) = &payment_data.payment_method_info {
308:                 payment_data.payment_attempt.payment_method_id = Some(pm_info.get_id().clone());
309:             };
310:             Ok(())
311:         } else {
312:             // Save card flow
313:             let save_payment_data = tokenization::SavePaymentMethodData::from(resp);
314:             let state = state.clone();
315:             let customer_id = payment_data.payment_intent.customer_id.clone();
316:             let payment_attempt = payment_data.payment_attempt.clone();
317: 
318:             let business_profile = business_profile.clone();
319:             let payment_method_type = resp.request.payment_method_type;
320:             let payment_method_billing_address = payment_method_billing_address.cloned();
321:             let payment_method_token = payment_data.payment_method_token.clone();
322: 
323:             let cloned_platform = platform.clone();
324:             logger::info!("Call to save_payment_method in locker");
325:             let _task_handle = tokio::spawn(
326:                 async move {
327:                     logger::info!("Starting async call to save_payment_method in locker");
328: 
329:                     let result = Box::pin(tokenization::save_payment_method(
330:                         &state,
331:                         connector_name,
332:                         save_payment_data,
333:                         customer_id,
334:                         &cloned_platform,
335:                         payment_method_type,
336:                         billing_name,
337:                         payment_method_billing_address.as_ref(),
338:                         &business_profile,
339:                         connector_mandate_reference_id,
340:                         merchant_connector_id.clone(),
341:                         vault_operation.clone(),
342:                         payment_method_info.clone(),
343:                         payment_method_token.clone(),
344:                     ))
345:                     .await;
346: 
347:                     if let Err(err) = result {
348:                         logger::error!("Asynchronously saving card in locker failed : {:?}", err);
349:                     } else if let Ok(tokenization::SavePaymentMethodDataResponse {
350:                         payment_method_id,
351:                         ..
352:                     }) = result
353:                     {
354:                         let payment_attempt_update =
355:                             storage::PaymentAttemptUpdate::PaymentMethodDetailsUpdate {
356:                                 payment_method_id,
357:                                 updated_by: storage_scheme.clone().to_string(),
358:                             };
359: 
360:                         #[cfg(feature = "v1")]
361:                         let respond = state
362:                             .store
363:                             .update_payment_attempt_with_attempt_id(
364:                                 payment_attempt,
365:                                 payment_attempt_update,
366:                                 storage_scheme,
367:                                 cloned_platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
368:                             )
369:                             .await;
370: 
371:                         #[cfg(feature = "v2")]

373:                             .store
374:                             .update_payment_attempt_with_attempt_id(
375:                                 &(&state).into(),
376:                                 &key_store.clone(),
377:                                 payment_attempt,
378:                                 payment_attempt_update,
379:                                 storage_scheme,

381:                             .await;
382: 
383:                         if let Err(err) = respond {
384:                             logger::error!("Error updating payment attempt: {:?}", err);
385:                         };
386:                     }
387:                 }
388:                 .in_current_span(),
389:             );
390:             Ok(())
391:         }
392:     }

396: #[async_trait]
397: impl<F: Clone> PostUpdateTracker<F, PaymentData<F>, types::PaymentsIncrementalAuthorizationData>
398:     for PaymentResponse
399: {
400:     async fn update_tracker<'b>(
401:         &'b self,
402:         state: &'b SessionState,
403:         mut payment_data: PaymentData<F>,
404:         router_data: types::RouterData<
405:             F,
406:             types::PaymentsIncrementalAuthorizationData,
407:             types::PaymentsResponseData,
408:         >,
409:         key_store: &domain::MerchantKeyStore,
410:         storage_scheme: enums::MerchantStorageScheme,
411:         _locale: &Option<String>,
412:         #[cfg(all(feature = "v1", feature = "dynamic_routing"))] _routable_connector: Vec<
413:             RoutableConnectorChoice,
414:         >,
415:         #[cfg(all(feature = "v1", feature = "dynamic_routing"))]
416:         _business_profile: &domain::Profile,
417:     ) -> RouterResult<PaymentData<F>>
418:     where
419:         F: 'b + Send,
420:     {
421:         let incremental_authorization_details = payment_data
422:             .incremental_authorization_details
423:             .clone()
424:             .ok_or_else(|| {
425:                 report!(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
426:                     .attach_printable("missing incremental_authorization_details in payment_data")
427:             })?;
428:         // Update payment_intent and payment_attempt 'amount' if incremental_authorization is successful
429:         let (option_payment_attempt_update, option_payment_intent_update) = match router_data
430:             .response
431:             .clone()
432:         {
433:             Err(_) => (None, None),
434:             Ok(types::PaymentsResponseData::IncrementalAuthorizationResponse {
435:                 status, ..
436:             }) => {
437:                 if status == AuthorizationStatus::Success {
438:                     (
439:                         Some(
440:                             storage::PaymentAttemptUpdate::IncrementalAuthorizationAmountUpdate {
441:                                 net_amount: hyperswitch_domain_models::payments::payment_attempt::NetAmount::new(
442:                                     // Internally, `NetAmount` is computed as (order_amount + additional_amount), so we subtract here to avoid double-counting.
443:                                     incremental_authorization_details.total_amount - payment_data.payment_attempt.net_amount.get_additional_amount(),
444:                                     None,
445:                                     None,
446:                                     None,
447:                                     None,
448:                                 ),
449:                                 amount_capturable: incremental_authorization_details.total_amount,
450:                             },
451:                         ),
452:                         Some(
453:                             storage::PaymentIntentUpdate::IncrementalAuthorizationAmountUpdate {
454:                                 amount: incremental_authorization_details.total_amount - payment_data.payment_attempt.net_amount.get_additional_amount(),
455:                             },
456:                         ),
457:                     )
458:                 } else {
459:                     (None, None)
460:                 }
461:             }
462:             _ => Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
463:                 .attach_printable("unexpected response in incremental_authorization flow")?,
464:         };
465:         //payment_attempt update
466:         if let Some(payment_attempt_update) = option_payment_attempt_update {
467:             #[cfg(feature = "v1")]
468:             {
469:                 payment_data.payment_attempt = state
470:                     .store
471:                     .update_payment_attempt_with_attempt_id(
472:                         payment_data.payment_attempt.clone(),
473:                         payment_attempt_update,
474:                         storage_scheme,
475:                         key_store,
476:                     )
477:                     .await
478:                     .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::PaymentNotFound)?;
479:             }
480: 
481:             #[cfg(feature = "v2")]
482:             {
483:                 payment_data.payment_attempt = state
484:                     .store
485:                     .update_payment_attempt_with_attempt_id(
486:                         &state.into(),
487:                         key_store,
488:                         payment_data.payment_attempt.clone(),
489:                         payment_attempt_update,
490:                         storage_scheme,
491:                     )
492:                     .await
493:                     .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::PaymentNotFound)?;
494:             }
495:         }
496:         // payment_intent update
497:         if let Some(payment_intent_update) = option_payment_intent_update {
498:             payment_data.payment_intent = state
499:                 .store
500:                 .update_payment_intent(
501:                     payment_data.payment_intent.clone(),
502:                     payment_intent_update,
503:                     key_store,
504:                     storage_scheme,
505:                 )
506:                 .await
507:                 .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::PaymentNotFound)?;
508:         }
509:         // Update the status of authorization record
510:         let authorization_update = match &router_data.response {
511:             Err(res) => Ok(storage::AuthorizationUpdate::StatusUpdate {
512:                 status: AuthorizationStatus::Failure,
513:                 error_code: Some(res.code.clone()),
514:                 error_message: Some(res.message.clone()),
515:                 connector_authorization_id: None,
516:             }),
517:             Ok(types::PaymentsResponseData::IncrementalAuthorizationResponse {
518:                 status,
519:                 error_code,
520:                 error_message,
521:                 connector_authorization_id,
522:             }) => Ok(storage::AuthorizationUpdate::StatusUpdate {
523:                 status: status.clone(),
524:                 error_code: error_code.clone(),
525:                 error_message: error_message.clone(),
526:                 connector_authorization_id: connector_authorization_id.clone(),
527:             }),
528:             Ok(_) => Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
529:                 .attach_printable("unexpected response in incremental_authorization flow"),
530:         }?;
531:         let authorization_id = incremental_authorization_details
532:             .authorization_id
533:             .clone()
534:             .ok_or(
535:                 report!(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError).attach_printable(
536:                     "missing authorization_id in incremental_authorization_details in payment_data",
537:                 ),
538:             )?;
539:         state
540:             .store
541:             .update_authorization_by_merchant_id_authorization_id(
542:                 router_data.merchant_id.clone(),
543:                 authorization_id,
544:                 authorization_update,
545:             )
546:             .await
547:             .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
548:             .attach_printable("failed while updating authorization")?;
549:         //Fetch all the authorizations of the payment and send in incremental authorization response
550:         let authorizations = state
551:             .store
552:             .find_all_authorizations_by_merchant_id_payment_id(
553:                 &router_data.merchant_id,
554:                 payment_data.payment_intent.get_id(),
555:             )
556:             .await
557:             .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
558:             .attach_printable("failed while retrieving authorizations")?;
559:         payment_data.authorizations = authorizations;
560:         Ok(payment_data)
561:     }
562: }

709:     ) -> RouterResult<PaymentData<F>>
710:     where
711:         F: 'b + Send,

714:             .payment_attempt

718:             .attach_printable("connector not found")?;
719: 
720:         let key_manager_state = db.into();
721: 
722:         // For PayPal, if we call TaxJar for tax calculation, we need to call the connector again to update the order amount so that we can confirm the updated amount and order details. Therefore, we will store the required changes in the database during the post_update_tracker call.
723:         if payment_data.should_update_in_post_update_tracker() {

731: 
732:                         let shipping_details = shipping_address

734:                             .async_map(|shipping_details| {

743:                             .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)

745: 
746:                         let shipping_address =

755:                                 storage_scheme,

758:

761:                     shipping_address_id: shipping_address.map(|address| address.address_id),
762:                     updated_by: payment_data.payment_intent.updated_by.clone(),
763:                     shipping_details,
764:         };
765: 
766:                         let m_db = db.clone().store;
767:                         let payment_intent = payment_data.payment_intent.clone();
768: 
769:                         let updated_payment_intent = m_db
770:                             .update_payment_intent(

773:                                 key_store,
774:                                 storage_scheme,
775:                             )
776:                             .await
777:                             .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::PaymentNotFound)?;
778: 
779:                         payment_data.payment_intent = updated_payment_intent;
780:                     } else {
781:                         router_data.response.map_err(|err| {
782:                             errors::ApiErrorResponse::ExternalConnectorError {
783:                                 code: err.code,
784:                                 message: err.message,
785:                                 connector,
786:                                 status_code: err.status_code,
787:                                 reason: err.reason,
788:                             }
789:                         })?;
790:                     }
791:                 }
792:                 Err(err) => {
793:                     Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::ExternalConnectorError {
794:                         code: err.code,
795:                         message: err.message,
796:                         connector,
797:                         status_code: err.status_code,
798:                         reason: err.reason,
799:                     })?;
800:                 }
801:                 _ => {
802:                     Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
803:                         .attach_printable("Unexpected response in session_update flow")?;
804:                 }
805:             }
806:         }
807: 
808:         Ok(payment_data)
809:     }
810: }

<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

## Quickstart 

<h3> Local Setup via Docker </h3>

```bash
# One-click local setup

git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch

cd hyperswitch

scripts/setup.sh
```
<details>
  <summary><strong>This script: </strong></summary>

  - Detects Docker/Podman  
  - Offers multiple deployment profiles:
    - **Standard**: App server + Control Center  
    - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

# Configs for deployments

## Introduction

This directory contains the configs for deployments of Hyperswitch in different hosted environments.

Hyperswitch has **3** components namely,

- router
- drainer
- scheduler
  - consumer
  - producer

We maintain configs for the `router` component for 3 different environments, namely,

- Integration Test
- Sandbox
- Production

To learn about what "router", "drainer" and "scheduler" is, please refer to the [Hyperswitch architecture][architecture] documentation.

### Tree structure

```text
config/deployments            # Root directory for the deployment configs
├── README.md                 # This file
├── drainer.toml              # Config specific to drainer
├── env_specific.toml         # Config for environment specific values which are meant to be sensitive (to be set by the user)
├── integration_test.toml     # Config specific to integration_test environment
├── production.toml           # Config specific to production environment
├── sandbox.toml              # Config specific to sandbox environment
└── scheduler                 # Directory for scheduler configs
    ├── consumer.toml         # Config specific to consumer
    └── producer.toml         # Config specific to producer
```

## Router

The `integration_test.toml`, `sandbox.toml`, and `production.toml` files are configuration files for the environments `integration_test`, `sandbox`, and `production`, respectively. These files maintain a 1:1 mapping with the environment names, and it is recommended to use the same name for the environment throughout this document.

### Generating a Config File for the Router

The `env_specific.toml` file contains values that are specific to the environment. This file is kept separate because the values in it are sensitive and are meant to be set by the user. The `env_specific.toml` file is merged with the `integration_test.toml`, `sandbox.toml`, or `production.toml` file to create the final configuration file for the router.

For example, to build and deploy Hyperswitch in the **sandbox environment**, you can duplicate the `env_specific.toml` file and rename it as `sandbox_config.toml`. Then, update the values in the file with the proper values for the sandbox environment.

The environment-specific `sandbox.toml` file, which contains the Hyperswitch recommended defaults, is merged with the `sandbox_config.toml` file to create the final configuration file called `sandbox_release.toml`. This file is marked as ready for deploying on the sandbox environment.

1. Duplicate the `env_specific.toml` file and rename it as `sandbox_config.toml`:

   ```shell
   cp config/deployments/env_specific.toml config/deployments/sandbox_config.toml
   ```

2. Update the values in the `sandbox_config.toml` file with the proper values for the sandbox environment:

   ```shell
   vi config/deployments/sandbox_config.toml
   ```

3. To merge the files you can use `cat`:

   ```shell
   cat config/deployments/sandbox.toml config/deployments/sandbox_config.toml > config/deployments/sandbox_release.toml
   ```

> [!NOTE]
> You can refer to the [`config.example.toml`][config_example] file to understand the variables that used are in the `env_specific.toml` file.

## Scheduler

The scheduler has two components, namely `consumer` and `producer`.

The `consumer.toml` and `producer.toml` files are the configuration files for the `consumer` and `producer`, respectively. These files contain the default values recommended by Hyperswitch.

### Generating a Config File for the Scheduler

Scheduler configuration files are built on top of the router configuration files. So, the `sandbox_release.toml` file is merged with the `consumer.toml` or `producer.toml` file to create the final configuration file for the scheduler.

You can use `cat` to merge the files in the terminal.

- Below is an example for consumer in sandbox environment:

  ```shell
  cat config/deployments/scheduler/consumer.toml config/deployments/sandbox_release.toml > config/deployments/consumer_sandbox_release.toml
  ```

- Below is an example for producer in sandbox environment:

  ```shell
  cat config/deployments/scheduler/producer.toml config/deployments/sandbox_release.toml > config/deployments/producer_sandbox_release.toml
  ```

## Drainer

Drainer is an independent component, and hence, the drainer configs can be used directly provided that the user updates the `drainer.toml` file with proper values before using.

## Running Hyperswitch through Docker Compose

To run the router, you can use the following snippet in the `docker-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
### Application services
hyperswitch-server:
  image: docker.juspay.io/juspaydotin/hyperswitch-router:latest # This pulls the latest image from Docker Hub. If you wish to use a version without added features (like KMS), you can replace `latest` with `standalone`. However, please note that the standalone version is not recommended for production use.
  command: /local/bin/router --config-path /local/config/deployments/sandbox_release.toml # <--- Change this to the config file that is generated for the environment.
  ports:
    - "8080:8080"
  volumes:
    - ./config:/local/config
```

To run the producer, you can use the following snippet in the `docker-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
hyperswitch-producer:
  image: docker.juspay.io/juspaydotin/hyperswitch-producer:latest
  command: /local/bin/scheduler --config-path /local/config/deployments/producer_sandbox_release.toml # <--- Change this to the config file that is generated for the environment.
  volumes:
    - ./config:/local/config
  environment:
    - SCHEDULER_FLOW=producer
```

To run the consumer, you can use the following snippet in the `docker-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
hyperswitch-consumer:
  image: docker.juspay.io/juspaydotin/hyperswitch-consumer:latest
  command: /local/bin/scheduler --config-path /local/config/deployments/consumer_sandbox_release.toml # <--- Change this to the config file that is generated for the environment
  volumes:
    - ./config:/local/config
  environment:
    - SCHEDULER_FLOW=consumer
```

To run the drainer, you can use the following snippet in the `docker-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
hyperswitch-drainer:
  image: docker.juspay.io/juspaydotin/hyperswitch-drainer:latest
  command: /local/bin/drainer --config-path /local/config/deployments/drainer.toml
  volumes:
    - ./config:/local/config
```

> [!NOTE]
> You can replace the term `sandbox` with the environment name that you are deploying to (e.g., `production`, `integration_test`, etc.) with respective changes (optional) and use the same steps to generate the final configuration file for the environment.

You can verify that the server is up and running by hitting the health check endpoint:

```shell
curl --head --request GET 'http://localhost:8080/health'
```

part.text:
Done. I've applied the minimal patch that prevents saving payment methods which lack support for future customer-present reuse.

**What changed:**
- **`crates/common_enums/src/enums.rs`** – Added `FutureUsage::is_on_session()`.
- **`crates/hyperswitch_domain_models/src/payments/payment_attempt.rs`** – Added `is_save_payment_method_not_supported_for_on_session()` to check whether a payment method type is in the configured unsupported list.
- **`crates/router/src/core/payments/operations/payment_response.rs`** – Before entering the save flow, the post-authorization handler now evaluates `setup_future_usage`. If it is `OnSession` and the payment method type is unsupported, saving is skipped.
- **`crates/router/src/configs/settings.rs`** – Added `OnSessionConfig` with a configurable `unsupported_payment_methods` map.
- **`crates/router/src/configs/secrets_transformers.rs`** – Wired the new config into the app settings.
- **Config files** (`development.toml`, `docker_compose.toml`, `integration_test.toml`, `production.toml`, `sandbox.toml`) – Populated the default unsupported list with `pay_later = ["klarna", "affirm"]`.

You can verify the result with `git diff HEAD`. The `common_enums` crate compiles cleanly; the full workspace build was not attempted because it has extensive pre-existing feature-flag errors unrelated to these changes.
